To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) neural networks appear to provide a good model of the evolution of behavior; (2) neural networks appear capable of providing a good model of behavior even when the organisms are so constrained that they cannot attain the optimal behavior; (3) neural networks provide an excellent framework for the study of neurobiology, particularly the neurobiology of behavior.

(1) neural networks can achieve behaviors that have fitnesses close to those predicted by evolutionary optimization models; and (2) this is true even when the neural network is very simple and the environment in which the neural network is embedded is relatively simple.

neural network models can be constructed that achieve fitnesses close to those of the evolutionary optimization models and, moreover, these neural networks have the same structure as the nervous systems of the organisms being modeled, suggesting that the neural networks may be biologically plausible.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a general theory for the relationship between evolution and the nervous system.
the evolution of neural network models for behaviors of organisms.
how organisms can achieve behaviors that are close to optimal in the face of the constraints imposed by evolution and ontogeny.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the evolutionary optimization models are useful for generating hypotheses about neural network structure and evolution and for suggesting directions for neurobiological experiments.
the evolutionary optimization model and neural network model are complementary, and that both are needed for a complete understanding of the evolution and ontogeny of behavior.
neural networks can be viewed as the evolutionary optimization models of behavior.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the neural network model is an effective alternative to the evolutionary optimization model, and that the neural network approach is a promising approach to understanding how evolution works.
neural network models can provide an alternative to evolutionary optimization models in the study of the evolution of behavior.
neural network models of animal behavior are not only feasible but may provide a more general and more powerful alternative to evolutionary optimization models.
The main takeaway from our work is that
neural networks may be sufficient to achieve behaviors that are near optimal in the Darwinian sense.
neural network models are a promising approach to understanding the evolutionary biology of behavior.
the neural network approach is a useful way to explore the evolution of behavior.
